thread:
maya: quick check — i'm about to land a terraform change that scopes per-model ConfigMaps into their own subpaths instead of a single shared CM in each namespace. this will change the checksum annotation key we compute. can this break the runtime hot-reload?

alex: can you paste the TF/manifest diff? main thing is whether we change the path the process watches or the annotation name that triggers rollout.

maya: sure, gist of the k8s template change:
```yaml
volumeMounts:
  - name: model-configs
    mountPath: /srv/models/{{ .Values.model }}/config
    subPath: {{ .Values.model }}
volumes:
  - name: model-configs
    configMap:
      name: model-configs-{{ .Values.env }}
```
we currently set annotation `configmap-checksum` on the sts template. TF PR switches to `checksum/configmap-model-<model>` so each model has an independent checksum.

tom: ok — runtime watches `/srv/models/*/config/*.json` via inotify. as long as files end up at that mountPath it'll pick up changes. issue: the rollout trigger we rely on is the `checksum/*` annotation on the statefulset, not inotify, because many infra changes require pod recycle. if TF changes the annotation key name, the helm/sts template generating the annotation needs to be updated too.

maya: exactly. my plan:
1) update TF to compute per-model checksums and add `checksum/configmap-model-<model>` annotation on sts template (helm).
2) keep a compatibility fallback for one deploy cycle: set old `configmap-checksum` to the first model's checksum so old-style monitors don't see a gap.
3) after canary and verification, remove fallback.

sara: timeline? i'm oncall tomorrow morning — if this causes unintended rollouts we could hit higher latencies. recommend canary in staging -> small prod shard -> full.

maya: canary tonight in `prod-canary` (2 pods). will open PR 4521 and mark for review.

alex: i'll look at runtime change: if we ever changed how the files get created (init-copy -> direct mount) in the past that broke inotify because copy doesn't trigger inotify events. ensure we preserve atomic writes or notify via the annotation-based rollout.

maya: good catch. plan is to KEEP direct mount (no init copy). i added a tiny wrapper to write to a tmp file then `mv` into place from the model side if we need atomicity.

tom: for helm, add this snippet to sts template to compute checksum per model (pseudo):
```yaml
annotations:
  checksum/configmap-model-{{ .Values.model }}: "{{ index .Files.SHA256 (printf \"configs/%s.json\" .Values.model) }}"
```
that will keep controllers reactive.

sara: tagging infra oncall: @alex @tom please monitor the canary. i'll keep an eye on latency dashboards and error budget.

deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: canary -> prod-canary at 2026-03-18T02:00Z (maints window). will post status.

alex: quick question — secrets: some models read an env KMS key reference. does the TF change affect secret sync? if the configmap name changes but secret name is the same we should be fine.

maya: no secret rename. but i'm adding an explicit `envFrom` reference in the template so the secret mount gets linked to the same checksum annotation family. will add in PR notes.

tom: small reviewer note: update the rollout docs under `deploy/docs/configmap-rollout.md` so SRE knows how to manually trigger a per-model restart: `kubectl patch sts/runtime-<model> -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt":"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}}}}}'`

maya: thanks — PR 4521: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/terraform/pull/4521 (draft). pinging @tom @alex for reviews.

tom: reviewing now, will approve if tests pass. :thumbsup:

sara: i'll watch the canary window and loop back in 30m. if anything odd, i'll revert.

maya: appreciate it. I'll post a short follow-up once canary finishes with health checks (latency, error rate, config validation).

deploy-bot: canary complete: all checks passed. promoting to prod in 10m unless blocked.
